title: Teacher loses preparation time to small administrative tasks that feel unrelated to teaching
job: Complete required admin work without displacing teaching, preparation and student support.
trigger: Attendance, forms, reporting or compliance tasks accumulate during the week.
surfaceComplaint: The admin tasks are individually tiny, but they eat the day.
believedCause: There is simply too much paperwork.
mechanism: The burden is not only total hours. Fragmented obligations interrupt higher-value teaching/preparation and often require duplicate entry across systems.

economics.painCostNote: OECD TALIS reports general administrative work as the largest named work-related stressor on average.

buyer.roiLogic: Recovered teacher time matters, but procurement economics are harder than private-sector markets.

distribution.acquisition: Start with one workflow controlled by a school.

intervention.offer: teacher admin time-map + one workflow automation

experiment.artifactRequest: time diary + screenshots/exports of one workflow
experiment.success: save ≥30 minutes/teacher/week on one workflow without more correction load
experiment.kill: procurement friction outweighs value or requirements cannot change locally

claims.text: OECD TALIS 2024 reports 52% of teachers identify general administrative work as a source of stress on average.
Administrative pain can be driven by interruption/context switching, not just raw hours.
